changes.text: Watching a long video to the end could leave you without the coins or the second chance it was offered for. It now pays out whenever the video actually played.
Being offered no video at all used to take the WATCH button away for the rest of the run, and could cost you one of the day's five videos. Neither happens now.

title: Safer names on the world board

changes.text: Names on the world board are checked before they are used, and you can report one that should not be there.

title: World leaderboard, an ad-free option, and a fuller board

changes.text: A world leaderboard: see the top players, where you rank, and choose the name everyone sees you under.
Remove the ads between levels with a one-time purchase. The videos you choose to watch for coins or a second chance keep working.
Levels now open with blocks already on the board, and special blocks start at level 5 instead of level 81.
Clearing two or more lines at once earns bonus lines towards the level goal, so setting up a double is worth more than two singles.
The hammer now smashes a three by three area instead of a single block.
Buying a power-up asks first, and shows what it costs and what you have left.
A finished video pays on a card you collect, and the coins fly into your purse.
Every level can now be finished with three stars; before this, more than half could not.
The video to keep a finished run going, and the video for extra coins, could stay unavailable for a whole session after the first one failed to load. They now keep trying in the background.
On some screens the home screen buttons overlapped each other.

title: A sweet new look, 200 new levels and a daily puzzle

changes.text: A brand-new candy look on every screen, with new effects, sounds, music and vibration.
200 new puzzle levels, for 260 in all, with stone, bomb and gift blocks to master along the way.
A daily puzzle with a reward every day and a treasure chest for playing all week.
Power-ups: undo a move, shuffle your pieces, or smash a block with the hammer.
Clear three or more lines at once for a big celebration.
Ads now come through ironSource, which can fill the offer to keep a finished run going from more than one ad network.
Choosing not to consent in the privacy prompt now also stops gameplay measurement, and a changed choice in Privacy Settings takes effect straight away instead of at the next launch.
Rewarded video and ads could be missing entirely, so the offer to keep a finished run going never appeared.
Ads and the offer to keep playing stopped appearing for some players.
Sharing a score now includes a link to the game, so whoever you send it to does not have to search the store.
A privacy settings option on the main menu, so you can change your ad choices at any time.
Endless mode: drop blocks onto an eight-by-eight grid and fill a row or a column to clear it. No timer, no levels, just your best score.
60 levels, each asking you to clear a number of lines inside a move budget, with up to three stars for finishing with moves to spare.
Combos that build a points multiplier while you keep clearing, with enough forgiveness that a streak survives one quiet move.
A best scores table showing your ten highest runs, alongside lifetime lines cleared and your best combo.
A run in progress is saved, so closing the game and coming back picks up exactly where you left off.
Plays completely offline, with no account and no sign-in.
